WHAT_CHANGED.CHANGE: Split 72K-line monolithic `synapse-agent` crate into 7 workspace crates: syn-core (foundation), syn-engine (indexer+graphrag+grace), syn-proxy (token-saving proxy), syn-run (autonomous runs), syn-skills (GRACE skills), syn-mcp (MCP server 48 tools), syn-cli (CLI+dashboard+tests).
Updated Dockerfile for 7-crate workspace COPY. Makefile and CI scripts already workspace-compatible via `cargo --workspace`.

Created 7 module shards (M-WORKSPACE-CORE through M-WORKSPACE-CLI), 7 verification shards, updated Phase-97.xml with completion evidence. graph-index.xml and verification-index.xml regenerated via `refresh --fix`.

Removed 6/7 `unreachable!()` calls (replaced with proper `anyhow::bail!`/`expect`). Removed `#[cfg(test)]` gates from Tracker fields and test helpers for cross-crate test access. Added tempfile/tokio dev-dependencies to workspace crates. Made `ToolProfile` visibility `pub` for downstream consumers.

WHY.REASON: Single-crate compilation was a bottleneck. 15 files exceeded 1,000 lines. Module boundaries were already clean but not enforced by the build system. The split enables parallel compilation, clearer ownership, and easier onboarding.

IMPACT.POSITIVE: Compile time improved via parallel crate compilation. 129 code modules remain intact with identical contracts. 155/157 tests pass (2 e2e require `cargo install` — pre-existing condition). GRACE verification: 127 modules synced, 1 advisory (7/1856 traceability gaps for new constant exports).
IMPACT.RISK: Cross-crate `#[cfg(test)]` helpers were a friction point — resolved by removing cfg gates from test-only public functions and struct fields.
